market: US (Nasdaq: AAOI) — manufacturing facilities in Sugar Land TX and Taipei Taiwan

evidence.claim: 1.6T first volume order >$200M from major hyperscale customer (March 9, 2026); shipments begin Q3 2026; first volume 800G data center order (December 10, 2025); $53M additional 800G single-mode order (March 30, 2026); total hyperscale backlog >$324M
evidence.source: Applied Optoelectronics press releases, GlobeNewswire, March 9 / December 10, 2025 / March 30, 2026

evidence.claim: FY2025 revenue $455.7M (+83% YoY); Q1 2026 revenue $151.1M (+51% YoY, +13% QoQ); full-year 2026 guidance raised to >$1.1B; CEO states actual demand $1.4-1.5B vs capacity-constrained $1.1B guide
evidence.source: AAOI 10-K FY2025 (SEC); Q1 2026 earnings call (BigGo Finance, May 7, 2026)

evidence.claim: In-house compound semiconductor fabrication: MBE + MOCVD in Sugar Land, Texas for GaAs (VCSEL) and InP (DFB/FP); laser chips manufactured exclusively at Sugar Land; no external laser sourcing — vertical integration from epi to finished module
evidence.source: AAOI 10-K FY2025 (SEC); Oxford Instruments partnership announcement (Compound Semiconductor News, January 2026)

evidence.claim: Texas facility expansion: 210,000 sq ft Sugar Land groundbreaking (February 13, 2026); two additional Pearland TX buildings (~388,000 sq ft) planned; targeting 650,000 units/month 800G/1.6T capacity by end 2026 (30% from Texas); Oxford Instruments InP process scale-up partnership
evidence.source: GlobeNewswire February 13, 2026; Compound Semiconductor News January 2026; Q1 2026 earnings call

evidence.claim: $20.85M Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund grant for Sugar Land expansion; 500+ jobs to be created — government validation of domestic compound semiconductor manufacturing importance

400mW narrow-linewidth DFB pump laser for silicon photonics and CPO introduced December 2025; samples to select customers; volume production late 2026 — direct play on co-packaged optics AI infrastructure trend

Microsoft accounts for 28.8% of FY2025 revenue; Digicomm (CATV distributor) 53.1%; top 10 customers ~98% of revenue — high customer concentration with both upside (Microsoft AI infrastructure) and risk (Digicomm/CATV cyclicality)

InP component supply shortage structural through at least 2027 per analyst consensus; TrendForce: AI datacenter optical transceiver market $26B in 2026; InP 400G/800G components ~50% behind demand at end 2025
evidence.source: TrendForce April 2026; TrendForce December 2025; multiple analyst reports 2026

what_could_weaken_view: Stock up 1,200% in 12 months to ATH $233.67 (May 13, 2026) at P/S 12.65x vs historical median 1.29x — most of the AI optical thesis is already priced in; incremental disappointment (capacity ramp delay, order slip) would be disproportionately punished

CATV segment ~44% of Q1 2026 revenue (Digicomm) — AAOI is more CATV than AI by revenue in 2025; cable capex cycle downturn or loss of Digicomm relationship would materially compress revenue growth narrative

Still not GAAP profitable — net loss $38.2M in FY2025, deepening to $14.3M in Q1 2026 despite 51% revenue growth; accumulated deficit $504M; $382M equity raise in Q1 2026 significantly diluted existing shareholders
Texas fab ramp slower than planned — 650,000 units/month by end 2026 requires flawless execution on two simultaneous construction projects; InP epitaxy scaling at this pace has no modern precedent

Microsoft customer concentration 28.8% — loss or significant reduction of Microsoft AI infrastructure orders would remove the primary AI-direct revenue signal; AAOI has not disclosed diversification beyond Microsoft + Amazon
CPO pump laser (400mW BH DFB) volume production late 2026 — sampling is confirmed but volume production timeline is management guidance; AI infrastructure CPO deployment pace is uncertain
